newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian carrier hopes for foreign shareholders.
newsitem.headline: Croatian carrier hopes for foreign shareholders.

text.p: Croatian state-owned carrier Croatia Airlines said on Friday it was hoping a major European airline might be interested in buying into it to spur the company's development.
The government has included a 13.97 million German mark, 27.10-percent stake in Croatia Airlines in the mass privatisation to be launched soon.

"This could be very positive for us," president Matija Katicic told Reuters. "People who get our shares may decide to put them on the market and someone like Lufthansa or Swissair might eventually buy them."

He said this would give the company stronger leverage in the competition against other airlines. Croatia Airlines flies to many major destinations in Europe and plans longer hauls once it buys bigger aircraft.
Its shares will be among assets in over 800 companies available to some 350,000 beneficiaries of the scheme in exchange for free vouchers through three auction rounds.
The shares could reach the market this autumn at the earliest.
Most beneficiaries of the scheme are expected to try to cash in on their windfall fairly quickly, though some might engage investment funds to manage their share portfolios.
The airline stake came from a swap between the government and the national oil company INA.

Some capital relations had still to be resolved between INA as a former shareholder that succeeded pre-1991 federal Yugoslav flag carrier JAT and Croatia Airlines, Katicic said but added that this should have no effect on its privatisation through vouchers.
Among its shareholders are Zagreb Airport with 14.2 percent and the state privatisation agency, controlling another 9.5 percent. Private investors have around eight percent.
